module_title: Gandhian Era (1919-1939) - Round Table Conferences, Poona Pact, and Tripuri Crisis
introduction: This advanced level focuses on an analytical study of British constitutional reforms (Govt of India Act 1935), the diplomacy of the Round Table Conferences, the representation of depressed classes (Poona Pact), the 1937 provincial elections, and the ideological clash between Subhas Chandra Bose and Gandhi in 1939.

core_concepts.title: Round Table Conferences (RTC)
core_concepts.description: Three conferences were held in London (1930, 1931, 1932). The Indian National Congress participated only in the Second RTC (1931), represented solely by Mahatma Gandhi. The conference failed over the minorities issue.

core_concepts.title: Communal Award and Poona Pact (1932)
core_concepts.description: British PM Ramsay MacDonald announced 'separate electorates' for the depressed classes. Gandhi undertook a fast unto death in Yerwada Jail against this. Finally, the 'Poona Pact' was signed between Ambedkar and Hindu leaders, agreeing to 'joint electorates' with reserved seats for depressed classes.

core_concepts.title: Government of India Act 1935
core_concepts.description: The longest British Act for India. It proposed an 'All India Federation', abolished Diarchy in the provinces granting 'Provincial Autonomy', and introduced Diarchy at the center.

core_concepts.title: Provincial Elections of 1937
core_concepts.description: Elections were held in 11 provinces under the 1935 Act. The Congress achieved massive success, forming governments in 8 provinces, signaling huge popular mandate against British rule.

core_concepts.title: Tripuri Crisis (1939)
core_concepts.description: During the INC Tripuri Session, Subhas Chandra Bose defeated Gandhi's preferred candidate, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, for the presidency. Due to ideological friction with Gandhi, Bose resigned and formed the 'Forward Bloc'.

important_entities.name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
important_entities.significance: Attended all three Round Table Conferences and strongly advocated for the political rights of the marginalized.

important_entities.name: Subhas Chandra Bose
important_entities.significance: Elected Congress President twice consecutively (Haripura 1938 and Tripuri 1939) before parting ways due to ideological differences with the Gandhian faction.

important_entities.name: Ramsay MacDonald
important_entities.significance: Announced the controversial 'Communal Award' in 1932, aiming to divide the Hindu society politically.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Note that Gandhi did NOT sign the Poona Pact himself (he was fasting). It was signed by B.R. Ambedkar on behalf of the depressed classes and Madan Mohan Malaviya on behalf of upper-caste Hindus.
The prominent Indian figures who attended all three Round Table Conferences were Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru. Congress boycotted the first and third.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Autonomy in Provinces, Diarchy at Center
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Simply remember that the 1935 Act swapped the 1919 system: it removed Diarchy from provinces to give them autonomy, and pushed Diarchy up to the central level.

exam_strategy_tips: Assertion-Reasoning questions frequently target the cause-and-effect relationship between the Communal Award, Gandhi's fast, and the Poona Pact.
A highly tricky and favored question: Who became the Congress President after Subhas Chandra Bose resigned during the 1939 Tripuri Crisis? (Answer: Dr. Rajendra Prasad).
